cards.design_implication: If designing observation or modeling strategies based on this abstract, one might conditionally prioritize models that accommodate outer magnetosphere emission for the majority of objects, while retaining flexibility for polar-cap emission in a minority of cases.
does_not_establish: Causal proof of the emission mechanism.
Detailed physical parameters defining the outer magnetosphere.
Universal applicability to all gamma-ray pulsars outside this specific sample.
cards.evidence_excerpt: For most of the pulsars, gamma-ray emission appears to come mainly from the outer magnetosphere, while polar-cap emission remains plausible for a remaining few.
limitations: The statement applies to 'most' pulsars in the specific catalog of 46 objects.
Polar-cap emission is noted as plausible for the remainder, indicating the mechanism is not exclusively outer magnetosphere.
cards.statement: For most pulsars in the catalog, gamma-ray emission appears to originate mainly from the outer magnetosphere.

cards.design_implication: When designing spectral analysis pipelines for similar datasets, one might conditionally include parameters for a power law with an exponential cutoff and set expected cutoff energy bounds around 1-5 GeV as a starting hypothesis.
does_not_establish: The exact physical cause of the cutoff.
Applicability to pulsars with different spectral characteristics outside this sample.
Precision of the measurement beyond the stated range.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The pulsed energy spectra can be described by a power law with an exponential cutoff, with cutoff energies in the range ∼1–5 GeV.
limitations: Scope limited to the 46 high-confidence pulsars in this specific Fermi LAT catalog.
Describes a mathematical fit to the data, not necessarily the intrinsic physical emission process.
cards.statement: Pulsed energy spectra in the sample can be described by a power law with an exponential cutoff, with cutoff energies in the range of approximately 1 to 5 GeV.

cards.design_implication: When defining detection thresholds or search strategies for gamma-ray pulsars, one might conditionally adjust expected sensitivity limits based on Galactic coordinates, anticipating lower sensitivity (higher limiting flux) near the Galactic plane.
does_not_establish: Exact flux limits for every coordinate.
How to fully correct for background variations in analysis.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The limiting flux for pulse detection is non-uniform over the sky owing to different background levels, especially near the Galactic plane.
limitations: Specific to the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) data mentioned in the text.
Does not provide quantitative values for the non-uniformity at every sky position.
cards.statement: The limiting flux for pulse detection varies across the sky due to differing background levels, particularly near the Galactic plane.
